discovery_review.rationale: Limited. Three retained aggregated search returns and 12 reported queries include neutral-looking product searches and meaningful limitation/challenge searches, including stale Claude excerpts, OpenCode 429/background reports, Orca dispatch/readiness reports and OpenWork licensing debate. However, reference-search-log.json has no per-query timestamps or exact tool request envelopes, no required-question/facet mapping, and the same generic conditional screening reason for all 74 candidate entries. The budget/source-cap stop explicitly leaves deeper implementation and runtime questions open. Included direct source bodies do not settle the surfaced issue reports at the pinned revisions. A full fces.semantic-review-dossier.v1 object with required question IDs, original request/governance and per-question screening was not supplied, so the empty question_reviews array is a structural limitation, not vacuous coverage success.

lineage_review.rationale: Adequate only for the memo's conservative source-observation scope. OpenAI help and Codex source are one organizational family; Anthropic Code/SDK/Cowork are another; code, README and tests within OpenCode or Orca are maintainer evidence rather than independent replication. OpenWork repository metadata advertises an OpenCode relationship, so conservative grouping avoids double-counting, but engine implementation was not traced. Distinct URLs and captured hashes establish neither independent outcomes nor authenticated acquisition. No product-performance or superiority inference is supported by these groups.
